text:
Marathon Petroleum stock has fallen 1.7% today and 7.4% over the past two weeks, tracking a sharp broader pullback in refinery stocks. The clearest trigger is a CNBC headline from today explicitly stating "The biggest money-making energy trade looks over"—the refinery sector's exceptional run has unwound, and investors are rotating out. This matters for Marathon because refiners profit when the gap between crude oil prices and finished fuel prices widens; that trade is reversing as the market reprices.

The timing coincides with a collapse in climate talks over the weekend that failed to restrict fossil fuels—which might seem positive for oil demand—but instead has triggered a rotation away from energy stocks entirely. Oil itself is trading around $90 a barrel, refineries are running at high capacity (95.7%), and fuel inventories remain elevated; none of that has changed enough to explain the magnitude of the sell-off in just the past week. The move appears driven by tactical profit-taking and sentiment shift in the sector rather than fundamental deterioration in refining economics.
